items.evidence: Even under the most generous gate (true post state, in-sample fit at the same layer, L15->L16): off-diag D21 error 35.9%, d3 21.6% (chain 6.6% / 4.7%). The R memory term gains only 0.3%. No slice-to-slice linear recursion can capture all-distinct memory (same conclusion as K3g).

items.title: Instead of a source bank, K = kM (~448) deterministic moment-matched particles; all channels from the cloud's empirical cumulants
items.what: Spherical design / cross-polytope particles, exact W and ReLU per particle; cost ~K/n u per layer.
items.evidence: Direct free-run (MLP #0, L15): cross-polytope 2048 — variance 3.0%, C off-diag 16%, d3 47%, K4d 183%, D21 74%; two-radius 4096 — nearly the same; 448 particles — variance 6.7%, D21 160%. Almost no difference between the deterministic design and random Gaussian (the design loses its advantage after the first ReLU). Chain: variance 0.14%, D21 6.6% — 20-50x worse. (Sampling was already dead.) dNTC's landmark part = Nyström/ISDF (dead).

items.source: Round 11: aggregated rank-k old kappa3 (T_old ~ sum sigma_a u_a x u_a x v_a, k ~ 230)
items.title: Aggregate rank-k CP of old kappa3, transporting the factors via B
items.what: All old sources combined into one CP; transport exact per factor; D21 = (U o U) diag(sigma) V^T.
items.evidence: No new run needed, using previously measured evidence: (1) the pooled old tensor's (a)|(bc) unfolding needs rank ~250 to reach 2% (32/128/256 -> 35/7.8/1.6%) — this is a lower bound on CP rank, the true CP would need far more rank; (2) capping CP rank to 2% in the chain needed ~8n columns; (3) the forum's rank-4608 CP channel gives 1.07e-7 (5x worse than the chain). The claimed 'rank-230 gives 2%' is actually the matrix rank of the D21 slice, not the tensor's CP rank. Each layer adds ~3n of new-rank birth, and re-compression (factored CP-ALS) costs ~2u per sweep.

items.title: Mixed forward/reverse or hierarchical contraction order for the young tier
items.what: Writing the young tier as a tensor network and searching all multiplication orders (opt_einsum + hand-built mixed orders).
items.evidence: Reproducing the ledger: transport 54.5u (108 products), D21 hub 50.5u (100 products), total 105.0u. The Hadamard has to be built first, and the code already fuses 2 right-factor contractions — that's the floor. The transport chain's cost is order-independent (all n×n). Reverse-style suffix precompute +75%, per-age separation +150%, batching is FLOP-neutral. Correction: A = P·R_b, R_b a fixed, full (non-diagonal) n×n birth matrix — A and P transport under the same left map (matches to 1e-14); the earlier claim that 'P^-1 A changes by 100-970%' was an ill-conditioned-inverse error (one Round 10 answer caught this). No cost gain: building A entry-wise still costs n^3. | The 4 outside Round 10/10b answers agree: 193 square products (39 P + 54 A + 100 D21) = 98.4u core, no order is cheaper. Astra: float64 numerical packing — the meter already counts float64 as double, zero gain (float16 = float32 = 1.0, no precision discount). One answer assumed a wrongly-prompted diag(a_b) and claimed 'A never needs to be built' — not applicable. Another answer's 49-55u claim was flagged by a different validator as a miscalculation.
items.next: Making the young tier cheap needs a representation change, not a reordering.

items.title: Cheap per-layer rule for κ4 (cheapening the Astra kernel, scale-mixture, C⊗C), the B2/WK12 half-cost family, λ refit, B1 memory carrier
items.what: Searching for the source of the 15-25% accuracy gap to the leaderboard.
items.evidence: New ReLU physics captures only 1-4% of the true κ4 at depth (from L8; 1.02 sanity at L2). Carrying the true κ4 linearly gives level 83-90%, pattern correlation 0.77-0.80 (chain 0.26-0.34). The chain's κ4 structurally lacks the (1,1,1,1) all-distinct part. Scale-mixture/C⊗C correlation ≤0.09. FB 2.0 +3.8%/+3.2%, λ 0.85 +1.8%/+1.0% (MLP#0/synth). D21 oracle: ×0.9999 in the feedback leg alone (cross-talk is dead), ×0.758 everywhere (exact κ3 slice = -24%). items.title: κ4 memory horizon: how much of the pattern do the last 1-4 steps of birth capture?
items.what: Extending opus12_k4_carry.py to carry the true κ4 linearly for only the last h steps (h=1..4); measuring pattern correlation and level.
items.evidence: κ4's deep pattern = carried memory (correlation 0.77-0.80 vs. chain 0.3); κ4 oracle -30%. | Result (q18_k4_horizon.py, N=1e6, MLP#0): erasing all memory at L-h and running the actual network forward h steps with Gaussian inputs, κ4 level at the decisive neuron, L12: h=1/2/3/4/6 → 2/6/12/18/35%, L16: 3/2/5/9/20%; pattern correlation with teacher L12 0.23/0.40/0.53/0.67/0.78, L16 0.20/0.41/0.59/0.65/0.77; best-scale errG4 h=2: 0.90/0.99, h=6: 0.37/0.63 — chain 0.19/0.21. The last 2 steps' births carry only 2-6% of κ4; even at 6 steps only 20-35%. κ4's memory is as long as κ3's: the young κ4 carrier is dead; the κ4 lever would need the full κ4 source chain — closed on cost grounds.

items.source: Own idea (after reading the 504aldo findings log F47, 25 Sep)
items.title: Refitting the disabled online mean correction (CORR_BETA) on v40fb's trajectory
items.what: v40fb has an online mean correction but it's disabled (NO_CORR=1): the β fitted for the old V16b hurts on the new base, so it's 'off until refit' — the refit was never done. F47's method: on a teacher-forced trajectory (with the true mean from the previous layer substituted in), ridge-fit each layer's fresh error from 13 per-neuron features (mu, var, sigma, alpha, phi, Phi, pred, D3, |D21| row-sum, K4, ...), then apply it online inside the loop. Cost is near zero (13 dot products/neuron/layer).
items.evidence: F47: on the V16b base, 3.65e-8 -> 2.52e-8 = 1.45x (5 train / 3 test MLPs, train~test, generalizes). Our older 'learned OUTPUT correction dead' finding was about a correction outside the loop — this is different. Risk: v40fb's regen/vecww base may already capture part of this; the gain is unknown. | Result (25 Sep, MLP#0, experiments/variants/estimator_q19corr.py + experiments/chain/q19_run.py): with the correction left off, the variant matches the shipped result exactly (2.2364e-8). In the teacher-forced run, each layer's fresh-error rms is 1.5-6.7e-5; with the 13 features, in-sample R² on the same network is only L3 0.15, L8/12/15 0.02 — about equal to the 13-parameter / 1024-neuron chance level (~0.013), i.e. no signal (F47 had R² 0.3-0.6 on the V16b base). v40fb's regen/vec+ww base has already absorbed the predictable part. Extra finding: forcing the mean to the true value drops final MSE from 2.24e-8 to 4.2e-9 — ~80% of the final error is accumulated mean error carried from earlier layers.
items.gate: If paired raw drops ≥3% on a held-out MLP, run Kaggle 100-MLP; fit only on local MLPs, never on the leaderboard

items.title: Breaking the one-for-one rule by reallocating rank/age-limit by layer (more cost at later layers)
items.what: Substituting the exact κ3 input (slice + d3) only in a specific layer window, to see where the gain accumulates.
items.evidence: Oracle (opus12_d21oracle.py + OPUS_OR_LMIN/LMAX, plain chain, MLP#0 / synthetic): all layers 0.608 / 0.715; layer ≥8 0.637 / 0.754; ≥12 0.704 / 0.863; ≥14 0.848 / 0.903; ≤11 0.884 / 0.837 (effects combine multiplicatively: 0.884×0.704≈0.62). The gain is spread across layers 8-16, not concentrated in the last 2-3 layers. And from an earlier measurement (notes K3ad/F-A5): even with the old sources kept fully dense and exact (no truncation at all), slice error only goes from 6.7% to 6.6%, final MSE only -3.9% (+19% cost) — the κ3 error doesn't come from compression, it's intrinsic to the birth of the K3 formulation (all-distinct post-ReLU κ3). So however rank/age-limits are reallocated, no large gain is possible.

items.source: Forum audit 25 Sep (Phase 1 teams SOX 18106, baltsat 18149, ely2sh 18176: skip work on inactive neurons)
items.title: Drop dead neurons from the source machinery (compaction)
items.what: Neurons with Phi ~ 0 contribute nothing to the next transport (their w1 column is ~0) and their own kappa3 rows barely affect the closure. Step 1 (accuracy oracle): set w1 := 0 for Phi < thr (experiments/variants/estimator_q20dead.py, knob Q20_DEAD_THR) and measure final MSE on the two teacher networks. Step 2 (only if step 1 is flat): compact the legs and products to the live neurons per layer (Strassen-compatible sizes), dropping dead rows on input and output.
items.evidence: Teacher statistics on MLP #0: Phi < 1e-3 for 6% (L8), 12% (L12), 17% (L16) of neurons; Phi > 1 - 1e-4 for 2% / 7% / 13%. Potential saving ~2 x dead fraction on each transport / contraction at deep layers, ~8-10% of the total (estimate, not measured). | Step 1 results (paired, MLP #0 / synthetic; experiments/variants/estimator_q20dead.py, Q20_DEAD_MODE bitmask): next-transport input only (w1 := 0) at Phi < 1e-4 / 1e-3 / 1e-2: -0.20% / +0.45%, -0.06% / +0.21%, -0.25% / -0.66%. Zeroing the dead neurons' OWN d3: x1.79 / x1.62 (catastrophic: their tiny means are tail-dominated, set by kappa3); zeroing their D21 rows/cols (d3 kept): +1.65% / +2.59% (not free). Dead birth columns (w2 := 0) + w1 at 1e-2: -0.37% / -0.59% (SAFE); at 3e-2: +8.5% / +7.9%. Adding always-on birth columns (Phi > 0.99): +0.77% / -0.79% (mixed); at 3e-2: +11% / +13%. Safe set: threshold Phi < 1e-2, drop dead neurons from the next-transport input rows and from newborn birth columns; keep d3 and D21 rows. Estimated young-tier saving (teacher dead fractions 0.05-0.25 at layers 5-16): 10 u (birth columns) to 16 u (+ transport rows) of 249 u, i.e. 4-6%; old tier / join could add a few u (not estimated). | STEP 2 (26 Sep, experiments/variants/v48_rowcompact.py = submissions/v48rc): input-side row compaction implemented (w1 := 0 at Phi < 1e-2; the next transport contracts over the live rows only, width padded to a multiple of 32 so Strassen L5 still applies: young legs + newborn A leg, Qc = WD Qc, Z/Zf thin stacks, transport-join basis and joiner projections; the covariance C slot keeps full width). Strassen pools now use one flat backing per (role, level), so the compacted widths add no memory. Exactness: compaction on vs off (same w1 := 0) differs by 6.5e-7 relative (width 512) / 1.05e-5 relative at the final layer of MLP #0 (f32 rounding amplified through the joins). Teacher pair vs v45: MSE -1.35% / -0.40%, util 0.2308 -> 0.2230 / 0.2227 (-3.4%). Submitted #332391; Kaggle runner B (100 MLPs) queued. | GRADED #332391 (v48rc): adjusted 4.6294e-9 (was 4.8066e-9, -3.7%), raw 2.1462e-8. Column-side oracles (experiments/variants/v48_coldrop.py): dropping the birth layer's dead neurons as HUBS (P columns := 0 kill every D3/D21 term of that hub; A columns, Rr / Ff rows := 0) x6.40 / x6.74 - their own tail-dominated kappa3 must propagate; zeroing dead rows/cols of the transported C x1.59 / x1.46. Only the input-row side is compactable.
items.gate: step 1: final MSE change <= +0.3% on both networks at thr >= 1e-3
items.next: Threshold sweep for w1 := 0 alone (0.02 / 0.03 / 0.05; the old 3e-2 kill included w2 := 0).
